title: IBM research finds agent memory works best as a calibrated dose
friendlyTitle: AI agents may need less memory than you think
summary: An IBM Research evaluation across eight models found that more agent memory is not automatically better: stronger models benefited from fuller guidance, weaker models often did better with a compact core plus retrieval, and saturated models showed little gain. In one reported result, curated retrieval raised task completion by 16.1 percentage points with only 5% more tokens.
friendlySummary: IBM researchers found that different AI models need different amounts of saved guidance. Giving an agent everything can sometimes make it worse.
whyItMatters: Agent builders can reduce cost and context clutter by measuring the right memory strategy per model instead of placing every past lesson into every prompt.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Careful memory settings can improve results while using fewer tokens and costing less.
